h1: The 6 Best Professional Electric Pruning Shears of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Pro Pruning Shears 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six professional electric pruning shears, from FELCO orchard tools to budget high-capacity models, compared on cut size, safety.
summary: The FELCO 834 is the best professional electric pruning shear: 1.6 inch capacity, Cut Shield finger safety and an F-Gold blade for full days in vines and orchards. The FELCO 2e brings the same safety idea for less. For big stated capacity on a budget, look at the Kebtek 40MM and the ANTTCTIG, and treat their claims with caution.
intro: Every listing leads with cutting capacity, and professionals learn to ignore it. A crew member works the same wrist motion thousands of times a day, so hand fatigue, blade quality and finger safety decide whether a shear stays in the truck long before the maximum branch size does. A tool that cuts a thick limb once and bruises your palm all afternoon is the wrong tool.

We reviewed six electric shears on paper and scored them on the Primea framework, looking at stated cut size, blade coating, battery setup and safety features. The order follows maker claims and reported crew use, with no field trials of our own, and prices appear as buckets. A pole lopper and a thinly described DEWALT were dropped as poor fits.

products.name: FELCO 834 Electric Pruning Shear, 1.6" Cutting Capacity, Cut Shield & F-Gold Blade for Professional Vineyard, Orchard, Farm Use
products.verdict: The tool built for a full day in the vines.
products.description:
The FELCO 834 is the shear the other five get measured against. It lists a 1.6 inch cutting capacity, the Cut Shield system and an F-Gold blade, and it is aimed at vineyard, orchard and farm crews. Cut Shield matters because an electric blade closes faster than a hand can pull away, so detecting a finger near the edge is a real injury control, not a feature to skim past.

It ranks first because it is the only pick marketed for sustained professional work, and it pairs that with the best-documented safety. The FELCO 2e drops the price tier from $500+ to $200 to $500, but its listing is aimed at lighter work.

Buy it if pruning is your income. The caveat is price: in the highest tier, it is far more tool than a weekend gardener needs.
products.idealFor: Orchard and vineyard professionals pruning all day.
products.skipIf: You prune a few hours per season.

products.name: FELCO 2e Electric Pruning Shears with Cut Shield Safety, F-Tech Coated Blade, 10.8V Lithium Battery
products.verdict: FELCO safety and blades in a lower tier.
products.description:
The FELCO 2e runs on a 10.8V lithium battery and carries the same Cut Shield safety idea as the 834, along with an F-Tech coated blade. Coated blades shed sap and resist rust, which keeps the cut clean and the motor cooler across a long row.

It takes second for a clear reason: the listing does not state a cutting capacity. For a professional that missing number is a genuine hole, since you cannot judge strain on the motor without it. The Kebtek 40MM costs in the same $200 to $500 tier and does state a size, though without any named safety system.

Buy it if documented finger protection from an established maker matters more than headline capacity. Confirm the maximum cut with FELCO before ordering, especially if your work includes thicker wood.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed large cut size.

products.name: Kebtek Electric Pruners Cordless Pruning Shear 40MM Professional
products.verdict: A 40mm cut without the FELCO price.
products.description:
Kebtek's 40MM is a cordless, professional-class shear with a stated 40mm cut, about 1.6 inches by the maker's own conversion, in the $200 to $500 tier. On paper it matches the FELCO 834's capacity for less money.

Paper is where the comparison ends. The listing names no safety system and no blade coating, and the spec sheet is thin, so you are trusting the cut number alone. That is why it sits behind both FELCOs even though it is the only other pick with a confirmed size in the professional range.

Buy it if you want near-professional capacity on a smaller budget and will use sensible hand habits. Skip it if documented safety is the priority, because nothing in the listing promises a finger-detection feature.
products.idealFor: Serious users wanting big cuts for less.

products.name: ANTTCTIG Electric Pruning Shears, 2.75'' Cut, 2 Batteries & Spare Blades
products.verdict: The most stated capacity and extras for the least money.
products.description:
The ANTTCTIG makes the boldest claim in the group: a 2.75 inch cutting diameter, with two batteries and spare blades in the box, in the $50 to $100 tier. A second battery is the extra that changes a working day, because you swap packs instead of waiting on a charger.

It ranks fourth because the capacity is the maker's claim, not a proven rating. A tool this cheap that quotes a bigger cut than either FELCO invites doubt about the motor and the blade steel that deliver it. Durability under daily use is unproven.

Buy it if you want swap-ready batteries and spare blades for the lowest outlay. Skip it if you need pro-grade longevity, and be cautious about pushing it near its stated limit, where a motor struggles first.
products.idealFor: Value buyers who need swap-ready batteries.

products.name: SEESII Electric Pruning Shears 4 Modes, 1.8" Cut Electric Pruners Cordless
products.verdict: Four cutting modes for varied branch sizes.
products.description:
SEESII gives you four cutting modes on a 1.8 inch cordless shear in the $50 to $100 tier. Modes are useful in practice: a gentle setting for twigs and softer growth reduces battery drain, while full power is kept for thicker wood.

It sits fifth because the ANTTCTIG gives more in the same bucket, namely two batteries and spare blades, while the SEESII listing gives no battery detail at all and names no safety system. Its 1.8 inch capacity is higher than the Kebtek 30mm and the FELCO 834's 1.6 inches, but that is a claim you cannot cross-check.

Buy it if you prune mixed branch sizes as a serious hobbyist or small-scale pro. Skip it if you want a bundled spare battery, since nothing says one is included.
products.skipIf: You want a bundled spare battery.

products.name: Kebtek 30mm/1.2" Electric Pruning Shears for Garden Care
products.verdict: Light-duty precision cuts, not thick-branch removal.
products.description:
The Kebtek 30mm is a garden-care shear with a stated cut of 30mm, or 1.2 inches, in the $100 to $200 tier. The smaller capacity shows its role: precision work on thinner growth, such as shaping shrubs and trimming canes.

It ranks last because the price does not match the spec. It costs more than the SEESII and the ANTTCTIG yet cuts the least of any shear here, and it lists no safety system or blade coating to compensate. A smaller cut is not a flaw by itself. The mismatch with price is.

Buy it if you do detail pruning in a garden and want electric assistance for thin stems. Skip it if you cut thick branches, because it is the least capable pick here and you will end up reaching for loppers.

whatMatters.detail: Cutting capacity is the thickest branch the blades can sever, quoted in millimeters or inches. Working near the limit strains the motor and dulls the edge fast, so buy above your usual branch size. Read the number in the title or specs, and be wary when a cheap shear claims more than a FELCO, as the ANTTCTIG does.

A safety system like FELCO's Cut Shield senses a finger near the blade and stops it. That matters because an electric blade closes faster than your hand can react. Only the FELCO 834 and 2e name one in this ranking. Look for the system by name in the listing, not a vague phrase like "safe design".

Blade coating decides how the edge behaves at hour six. Coated blades such as FELCO's F-Gold and F-Tech resist sap and rust and glide through green wood, while plain steel gums up and drags. If a listing names no coating, assume plain steel. Check the title and bullets for the coating name, and budget for spare blades.

A second battery lets you keep cutting while the first charges, and spare blades extend the tool's life. Both change a long workday more than a few millimeters of capacity do. The ANTTCTIG ships with two batteries and spare blades. Check the box contents in the listing before you assume anything comes with the shear.

Pruning repeats the same motion thousands of times, so weight and balance decide whether your hand survives the shift. Professional tools tune the grip and balance for that. Listings rarely quantify it, so compare any weight stated and read owner feedback about hand strain, especially on the cheaper shears with a big claimed capacity.

faq.q: Can I use these on thick branches?
faq.a: Only within the stated capacity, such as 1.6 inches on the FELCO 834 or 40mm on the Kebtek. Beyond that, switch to a pruning saw or loppers, because forcing a cut stalls the motor and dulls the blades.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying on capacity alone and ignoring safety and fatigue. The ANTTCTIG quotes a large number, but the FELCO 834 adds Cut Shield and a coated blade, which protect your fingers and your hand across a full day.

faq.q: Is the FELCO 834 worth it over the Kebtek 40MM?
faq.a: For daily professional use, yes. You get Cut Shield and an F-Gold blade the Kebtek 40MM never names. For occasional use, the Kebtek matches the stated 1.6 inch size for less money in the $200 to $500 tier.
For long days, yes. A second battery means you swap and keep working. The ANTTCTIG includes two, while the FELCO 2e and SEESII list no spare. Charge both before heading out to the rows.

faq.q: How do I maintain the blades?
faq.a: Clean sap off the blades after use with a cloth and keep the tool dry. Replace or sharpen blades when cuts turn ragged. The ANTTCTIG ships with spare blades, and FELCO coatings like F-Gold shed sap more easily.
They can be, with gloves and clear fingers. Cut Shield on the FELCO 834 and 2e detects a finger near the blade and adds a layer of protection, but no electric shear removes the need for care.

finalTake: For professional work, the FELCO 834 is the shear to buy: 1.6 inch capacity, Cut Shield and a coated blade built for full days. The FELCO 2e is the safety-first step down, though you must confirm its cut size. The Kebtek 40MM and ANTTCTIG offer capacity for less, with thinner specs and unproven durability. Choose protection and fatigue over the biggest number.
